key_headlines.title: New Bank of Korea Governor Attends First F4 Meeting, Confirms Crisis Response Capability
key_headlines.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul chaired an expanded macroeconomic and financial meeting with the new Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song, confirming sufficient crisis response capacity despite ongoing financial and foreign exchange volatility from Middle East tensions.

key_headlines.title: Securities Firms Project Two Rate Hikes This Year Amid Rising Oil Prices and Strong GDP Growth
key_headlines.summary: Following the Middle East war extending beyond two months and Q1 GDP growth significantly exceeding expectations at 1.7%, brokerage houses are forecasting two base rate increases in 2026, with some projecting hikes in August and November.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Drops 1.38% to 6,598 Amid High Oil Prices and Fed Rate Hold
key_headlines.summary: The KOSPI fell below the 6,600 mark as international crude prices surged past $100 and the Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark rate at 3.50-3.75%, with the won-dollar exchange rate rising to 1,483.3 won.

key_headlines.title: LG Energy Solution Signs 10 Trillion Won Battery Supply Contract with BMW
key_headlines.summary: LG Energy Solution secured a major 10 trillion won electric vehicle battery supply deal with German automaker BMW, marking a potential turnaround for Korea's secondary battery industry after facing demand challenges.

key_headlines.title: Seoul Apartment Rent Transactions Exceed 70%, Reflecting Shift from Jeonse to Monthly Rent
key_headlines.summary: Monthly rent transactions in Seoul apartments have surpassed 70% for the first time in 2026, as the scarcity of jeonse (key money deposits) forces residents to leave Seoul and drives up prices in Gyeonggi Province.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economic leadership convened for the first expanded macroeconomic and financial meeting under new Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song, with Deputy Prime Minister Koo Yun-chul affirming sufficient crisis response capacity despite heightened risks. Key concerns include the Iran-Middle East war ceasefire negotiations at an impasse, widening downside economic pressure, accelerating inflation, and supply chain disruptions. The government is maintaining 24-hour market monitoring through an emergency response system. Despite external uncertainties from the Fed's rate hold and Middle East tensions, Korean officials expressed confidence in their ability to manage financial and foreign exchange market volatility.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Multiple securities firms are now forecasting two base rate hikes within 2026, driven by surging international oil prices exceeding $100 per barrel and stronger-than-expected Q1 GDP growth of 1.7% quarter-over-quarter. The Fed's three consecutive rate holds have created persistent uncertainty in U.S. monetary policy, with some Fed officials expressing dissent regarding dovish language. The European Central Bank also maintained rates while expressing concerns about potential stagflation similar to the 1970s oil shocks. Next week's economic data releases will include April inflation figures and March current account statistics, with expectations for a record trade surplus driven by semiconductor exports.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI declined 1.38% to close at 6,598.87 on May 1, falling below the psychologically important 6,600 level due to surging crude oil prices and the Fed's hawkish rate hold decision. The won-dollar exchange rate strengthened to 1,483.3 won, reflecting foreign exchange volatility. Individual investors purchased 1.187 trillion won while foreign investors sold 1.4618 trillion won net. Leveraged ETFs on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix showed strong activity, with new 2x leverage products launching on May 22, expanding options for domestic investors previously limited to cumbersome overseas trading channels.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's April exports exceeded $80 billion for the second consecutive month, driven by the semiconductor super-cycle, offsetting declines in internal combustion engine vehicle exports. LG Energy Solution secured a landmark 10 trillion won battery supply contract with BMW for cylindrical 100GWh EV batteries, signaling potential recovery for Korea's secondary battery sector. Massive lithium reserves equivalent to 130 million electric vehicles were discovered in the United States, potentially reshaping global battery supply chains. Green vehicle exports grew 23% for electric vehicles and 8.6% for hybrids, though unable to offset the 17% decline in traditional car exports amid prolonged Middle East tensions affecting energy trade.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's housing market is experiencing a dramatic shift from jeonse (lease with key money deposit) to monthly rent transactions, with monthly rent accounting for over 70% of all transactions in the first quarter of 2026. The scarcity of jeonse apartments is forcing Seoul residents to relocate to Gyeonggi Province, where apartment deposit values are rising 4.19% in some areas despite declining overall jeonse inventory. The government is reviewing enhanced transparency measures, including adding diagnostic pricing information to the real estate transaction disclosure system to prevent empty jeonse risks. Political candidates are focusing on housing policy reforms, with differing approaches to redevelopment incentives and supply expansion strategies.
sections.International Economy: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell announced his intention to remain on the Fed Board after his term expires, citing ongoing Trump administration political pressures and investigation into the Fed's headquarters renovation as reasons for staying. The FOMC recorded its largest dissent since 1992, with four members opposing the rate hold decision, highlighting unprecedented policy disagreement within the central bank. Powell described current economic conditions as unprecedented and difficult, acknowledging that supply shocks pose potential risks to both inflation and unemployment. U.S. stock markets closed mixed amid high oil prices and monetary policy uncertainty, with the Fed continuing to monitor pandemic aftereffects, Ukraine war impacts, tariffs, and energy prices in its policy decisions.
sections.AI & Economy: The artificial intelligence industry is transitioning from pure performance competition to efficiency and profitability-driven competition, with market focus shifting from 'smartest AI' to 'cost-effective working AI' as major tech companies seek practical business applications. Big Tech companies reported first-quarter earnings surprises with increased AI infrastructure investments, though profitability concerns regarding massive AI capital expenditures remain. CPU-related stocks are gaining attention as AI agent demand increases, shifting focus from GPUs and memory semiconductors, particularly following Intel's stronger-than-expected earnings. The government is launching a public participation 'National Growth Fund' this month focused on AI and semiconductor investments, though investors remain cautious given past policy funds achieving only 2% annual returns.
sections.Others: Spirit Airlines, a major U.S. low-cost carrier, failed to reach a bailout agreement with the Trump administration and faces operational suspension due to bankruptcy risks. Apple's Mac Mini is experiencing high demand for AI agent applications due to its superior M4 chip AI performance and favorable pricing from 2024, effectively resulting in a 300,000 won price increase. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are accelerating their transition to advanced NAND flash manufacturing processes, with NAND emerging as a critical component for AI inference and becoming a major revenue source comparable to DRAM. Oil prices have risen for five consecutive weeks, with Dubai crude reaching $107.5 per barrel, gasoline at $129.7 per barrel, and diesel at $172.4 per barrel, continuing upward pressure on fuel costs.
